title: Titan: A World of Methane Lakes
objective: After this level you can describe Titan’s thick atmosphere and liquid methane lakes.
summary: Saturn’s largest moon has a thick nitrogen atmosphere and lakes of liquid methane; the Huygens probe landed there in 2005.

cards.headline: It rains on Titan. Just not water.
cards.body: Titan has clouds, rain, lakes and seas. It's a weather report that sounds almost like home, right up until you check what's falling from the sky.

cards.headline: A moon with weather
cards.body: Titan is Saturn's largest moon, bigger than the planet Mercury. It's also the only moon with a thick atmosphere, made mostly of nitrogen, just like the air you breathe. Its clouds rain methane, which gathers in lakes and seas of liquid methane and ethane. Why not water? At about −179 °C, Titan is far too cold for liquid water. Pack a raincoat. And a very warm sweater.

cards.headline: Earth's strange cousin
cards.body: Those methane lakes make Titan special. Apart from Earth, it's the only world known to have stable liquid on its surface. Even Europa, with all its water, keeps its ocean hidden under a shell of ice. A place like Titan deserved a visit, and in 2005 it got one: the Huygens probe landed there, the first landing ever on a world in the outer solar system. Of all the far-off places to touch down first, we picked the one with lakes.
